AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agri- business Accounts? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agri- business Accounts.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agri- business Accounts.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Agri- business Accounts.

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Breeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Disease Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. B — 100 °C

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.

8. C — Ice melting to water

9. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.

11. B — Glucose and oxygen

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Livestock Nutrition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Health: Disease Control; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
